h1: The 8 Best Extra Large Fireproof Safes for Documents, Cash and Valuables, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Extra Large Fireproof Safes: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 extra large fireproof safes from 4 to 9.8 cubic feet, scored on fire rating claims, door build, bolts and lock type.
summary: The Mitlvge 35-Minute fireproof safe is the best extra large safe here because its listing cites a UL standard and SGS certification for a 35 minute rating at 1700 degrees F. The 9.8 cubic foot biometric safe is the pick for the largest capacity, the 5.2 cubic foot combination safe has the thickest listed door, and the Omethey adds a deposit slot.
intro: Fire ratings on consumer safes are the most inflated numbers in home security. A listing that says fireproof can mean anything from a laboratory-tested 30 minute rating to a layer of insulation that no one has measured. The first thing to look for is who verified the claim: a named standard, a named test lab, or nothing at all.

Eight extra large safes are ranked here, from 4.0 to 9.8 cubic feet. Each is scored on how well the fire claim is documented, the door and bolt build, the lock type and the capacity. We read the listings; we did not burn anything, so these are paper judgments about documentation, not lab results.

products.name: Mitlvge 35-Min Real Fireproof Safe, 23.4" Tall
products.verdict: A 35 minute rating at 1700 degrees F backed by a cited UL standard and SGS certification.
products.description:
The Mitlvge 35-Min safe stands 23.4 inches tall and weighs 45 lbs. Its listing cites a UL standard and SGS certification for 35 minutes at 1700 degrees F, with 3 locking bolts of 0.98 inch and pre-drilled holes closed with fireproof sealing plugs.

It ranks first because a named test standard and a named certification body are the strongest evidence a listing can offer. The sealed pre-drilled holes show the maker thought about fire entering through the bolt-down points, which is where many safes leak heat. Weight is modest for an extra large safe, so bolting it down matters. It is the most expensive of the 5 cu ft class.

Buy it if a documented fire rating matters most. Skip it if you want maximum capacity.
pros: Named UL standard and SGS cert
products.idealFor: Documents and media that must survive a house fire.

products.name: 9.8 Cu Ft Extra Large Biometric Fireproof Waterproof Safe
products.verdict: 9.8 cubic feet and 124 lb with 8 locking bolts and fingerprint access with a key backup.
products.description:
The biggest safe in this ranking offers 9.8 cu ft, weighs 124 lbs and has 8 locking bolts, 5 live and 3 dead. Access is by fingerprint with a key backup.

It takes second place because it combines capacity and mass: 124 lb is heavy enough to resist a casual walk-off, and eight bolts spread the load around the door. Live bolts move with the lock, and dead bolts sit fixed in the door, so both resist prying. The fireproof and waterproof claims in the title are not backed by a named standard in the listing we reviewed, so treat them as marketing until you see paperwork.

Buy it if you need to store firearms-sized or bulky items and want serious weight. Skip it if documented fire testing is your top need.
cons: Fire and water claims not documented
products.idealFor: Bulky valuables needing a heavy safe.
products.skipIf: You need a named fire standard.

products.name: 5.2 Cu Ft Large Fireproof Safe with Combination Lock
products.verdict: A 67mm reinforced door, four 20mm round bolts and three unlock methods with alarm lockout.
products.description:
This 5.2 cu ft safe has a 67mm reinforced door, 4 round locking bolts of 20mm, three unlock methods and a tiered alarm lockout.

A 67mm door is the thickest listed in this ranking, and thickness is both a pry-resistance and an insulation feature. Tiered lockout means repeated wrong codes trigger longer delays and an alarm, which stops guessing. It ranks third because the listing gives no named fire rating, and a thick door is no proof of one.

Buy it if door strength and flexible access matter. Skip it if you require a certified fire rating.
products.idealFor: Security-minded buyers in the mid range.
products.skipIf: You want a certified fire test.

products.name: 31.5" Large Fireproof Waterproof Safe with Biometric Access
products.verdict: 85 lb with a 35 minute fire claim at 1800 degrees F and sub-one-second fingerprint access.
products.description:
This 31.5-inch safe weighs 85 lbs, claims 35 minutes at 1800 degrees F, and opens in under a second with a fingerprint reader that stores 29 prints. It ships with no pre-drilled mounting holes.

The lack of mounting holes is a stated tradeoff: it preserves the fire seal but means you cannot bolt it down without drilling yourself. At 85 lb it is heavy, but a determined thief can still move it. Twenty-nine stored prints suit a family or a small business. It ranks fourth because the fire claim names no standard.

Buy it if you want fast biometric access and a sealed body. Skip it if you must bolt it to the floor.
pros: Sealed body with no pre-drilled holes
cons: Cannot be bolted down as supplied
Fire claim not tied to a standard

products.name: Mitlvge 23.62" Tall 5.0 Cu Ft Extra Large Home Safe
products.verdict: 5.0 cubic feet with a 50mm steel door and a bundled A4 fireproof bag rated 30 minutes at 1700 F.
products.description:
The Mitlvge 5.0 cu ft stands 23.62 inches tall, weighs 38.8 lbs and has a 50mm steel door with 3 removable steel shelves. A bundled A4 fireproof bag is rated for 30 minutes at 1700 degrees F.

The bag is a thoughtful extra for passports and drives, but note that the 30 minute claim is for the bag, not the safe body. The safe itself offers a thick door at a modest weight. It ranks fifth because the body's fire rating is not documented separately.

Buy it if you want the bag included and a thick door. Skip it if you need a fire claim for the body itself.

keySpecs.label: Bonus
keySpecs.value: A4 fireproof bag, 30 min at 1700 F

products.skipIf: You need a rated safe body.

products.name: Omethey 5.0 Cu Ft Extra Large Safe with Deposit Slot
products.verdict: A double-door independent design with a front deposit slot, four live bolts and a backlit keypad.
products.description:
The Omethey has 5.0 cu ft, a double-door independent design, a front deposit slot, 4 solid live bolts and a backlit keypad.

The deposit slot lets cash go in without opening the door, a feature for small businesses and shared households. Double doors separate valuables from everyday items. The compromise is that independent doors add hinges and seams, and the listing lacks a fire rating.

Buy it if you drop cash or envelopes regularly. Skip it if fire protection is your top need.
cons: More seams than a single door
products.skipIf: You want a certified fire rating.

products.award: Most Interior Space for the Price
products.name: 6.2 Cu Ft Large Home Safe with 3 Removable Shelves
products.verdict: 6.2 cubic feet with a 42mm door and three 20mm bolts at only 39.6 lb.
products.description:
The 6.2 cu ft safe has a 42mm thick door, 3 locking bolts of 20mm and 3 removable steel shelves, at 39.6 lbs.

It offers the second-largest interior here, but at 39.6 lb it is lightweight for its size, which hints at thin body walls. The door is thinner than the Mitlvge's 50mm, and no fire rating is listed. Bolt it down if you buy it.

Buy it if you want maximum space on a limited budget. Skip it if you need documented fire protection.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who need interior room.
products.skipIf: You want a heavy, rated safe.

products.name: WASJOYE 4.0 Cu Ft Large Cabinet Safe with Type-C Port
products.verdict: A 4.0 cubic foot cabinet with two fireproof drawers, a 20mm bolt and a Type-C emergency power port.
products.description:
The WASJOYE is a 56.11 lb cabinet safe of 4.0 cu ft with 2 fireproof drawers, a 20mm anti-pry door lock bolt and a Type-C port for emergency power.

The Type-C port is a thoughtful detail: if the batteries die, you can power the keypad from a power bank. Drawers organise small items. It ranks last because it is the smallest, with only one bolt listed, and the fire claim is unspecific.

Buy it if you want drawers for paperwork and a power backup. Skip it if you need a large interior.

methodology.title: Fire claim documentation
methodology.description: Named standards, test labs and temperature-time claims were weighed above bare fireproof wording.

methodology.title: Door and bolts
methodology.description: Door thickness, bolt count and bolt type were compared as signs of pry resistance.

methodology.title: Capacity and weight
methodology.description: Interior volume and mass were assessed together, since a large light safe is easy to carry off.

methodology.title: Lock and access
methodology.description: Biometric, keypad, combination and key backup systems were scored for reliability and speed.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Safes were placed in the $100 to $200, $200 to $500 and $500 plus brackets against their documentation.

whatMatters.detail: A claim backed by a named standard or lab, like the UL standard and SGS on the Mitlvge 35-Min, is stronger than the word fireproof. Look for a temperature, a duration and a body that tested it. Ratings are typically for documents, and digital media can fail at lower temperatures.
A thick door and several large bolts resist prying. Live bolts move with the lock, and dead bolts sit fixed in the door. Look for at least three bolts of 20mm or more.
A safe under about 100 lb can be carried out by two people. Anchor bolts into a concrete floor stop that. The 31.5 inch safe lacks mounting holes by design, so plan for that.
Fingerprint locks are fast but need batteries and a key backup. Combination locks are mechanical and slower. Keypads can lock out after wrong attempts, as the 5.2 cu ft safe does.
Cubic feet only matter if the shelves fit your items. Removable shelves, as on the 6.2 cu ft model, flex the layout. Measure the tallest object you plan to store.

faq.q: Is a fire rating a guarantee?
faq.a: No. A rating means contents stayed below a temperature in a lab test for a set time. Real fires vary, and digital media is more sensitive than paper.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a safe?
faq.a: Trusting the word fireproof. Look for a named standard and a time at temperature. Then anchor the safe, since a light one can be carried off.

faq.q: Is the Mitlvge 35-Min worth it over a cheaper 5 cu ft safe?
faq.a: If a documented rating matters, yes. The cited UL standard and SGS certification give real information, which cheaper listings do not.
Place it in a corner on a concrete floor and bolt it down if it has mounting holes. Use anchors designed for the floor type.

faq.q: What happens if the batteries die?
faq.a: Most keypad safes have a key backup, and the WASJOYE includes a Type-C emergency power port. Replace batteries once a year.
Paper-rated protection is not always safe for drives, discs and photos. Look for a media rating or store backups elsewhere.

finalTake: The Mitlvge 35-Min Real Fireproof Safe is the best extra large safe here, because its listing names a UL standard and SGS certification for a 35 minute rating at 1700 degrees F. The 9.8 cubic foot biometric is the pick for sheer size and mass, and the 5.2 cubic foot combination safe has the thickest door. Always anchor the safe, and store irreplaceable media off-site as well.
